clue.text: Beastly African cases for old doctor

parts.note: a hippo is a big African beast
crates are packing cases

explanation.surface: A safari vet treats wild animals that are boxed up for shipping.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek physician of antiquity is called the father of medicine, hence an ancient doctor.

clue.text: Relative hammered nail on top of wardrobe

indicators.note: something hammered is beaten out of shape, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: 'top of' keeps only the first letter of 'wardrobe'

parts.note: the first letter of wardrobe

explanation.surface: A relative bangs a nail into the top of a wardrobe during some DIY.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On top of' just places the W after the rearranged letters, since in a down entry it sits below them.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-law is a relation by marriage, such as a spouse's parent or sibling.

clue.text: Cheers coming after success with a sauce

parts.note: a pass is success in an exam
taken as written
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: A toast is raised after a triumph, with a dish served in a sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming after' puts the thanks after the success and the A; ta is an informal British thank-you.
explanation.definitionFit: Passata is sieved uncooked tomato purée used as a base sauce in Italian cooking.

clue.text: Seed overcome, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: the phrase asks us to listen to the word rather than read its spelling

parts.note: to overcome is to conquer, which is pronounced the same as the seed's name

explanation.surface: Something about a seed is defeated, or so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: A conker is the shiny brown seed of the horse chestnut tree, used in a British children's game where one is swung on a string to smash another.
explanation.definitionFit: A conker is literally the seed of the horse chestnut tree.

clue.text: A paper's ending with fully-developed framework

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the last letter of paper
mature means fully grown or developed

explanation.surface: A newspaper's closing piece comes with a fully worked-out structure.
explanation.definitionFit: An armature is a supporting framework, such as the skeleton inside a sculpture.

clue.text: Stylish English member, soldier

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a limb is a member of the body
a soldier ant, so a soldier can be an ant

explanation.surface: A smart English member of a regiment cuts a fine figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Member is a limb here, and soldier is the insect caste, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant and stylish both describe graceful, fashionable appearance; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Crick, say, tedious person

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literal discomfort below the head, of which a crick is one example
second meaning: an idiom for an irritating, wearisome person

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crick' could suggest the DNA scientist, but it is the stiff-muscle complaint, and 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A crick is a stiff ache below the skull, and the same phrase is a common idiom for an annoying bore.

clue.text: After party, spoon out jam

parts.note: Con is short for the Conservative Party
to spoon out food is to serve it

explanation.surface: Once the party is over, someone ladles out the jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After party' places the party first, ahead of the serving.
explanation.definitionFit: A conserve is a preserve made of whole fruit and sugar, a kind of jam.

clue.text: The new stadium freshened up one side of London

indicators.note: something freshened up has been redone and reworked, so these letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: every letter taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A refurbished stadium has given a London football team a new look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' is a sports team, not a geographical half of the city; this club moved into the London Stadium in 2016.
explanation.definitionFit: West Ham United is a London football club, and in sport a side is a team.

clue.text: Titan finally scratching back

indicators.note: scratching means striking out, and back points to the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: finally means at last

explanation.surface: A giant at last scratches an itch on his back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' is not selecting a last letter here; it is the phrase at last, which then loses its own end.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Atlas was one of the Titans, condemned to hold up the heavens.

clue.text: Feeling less, yours truly getting hit

parts.note: with less feeling, one is more numb, so numb-er
one is a pronoun for oneself, the speaker

explanation.surface: Someone is struck and goes numb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' must be read as the comparative of numb, with the B sounded silently.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart-topping record is a number one, the biggest kind of hit.

clue.text: Shop original man from South Africa?

parts.note: original means new, novel
SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
gent is short for gentleman

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a shop's founder came from South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a newsagent is a shop selling papers, magazines and sweets; the word names both the shop and its keeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsagent, or newsagent's, is a local British shop selling newspapers and confectionery.

clue.text: Equally determined to produce benefit

parts.note: as, as in as tall as, expresses equality
set on something means determined

explanation.surface: Being equally resolved yields an advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful quality or advantage, in other words a benefit.

clue.text: Absolutely not certain of earnings, only some shown

indicators.note: only a part of the words that follow is on display, so the answer sits within them

parts.note: runs from the end of certain through of into the start of earnings

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure what they earn, and only part of the payslip is shown.
explanation.walkthrough: No fear is British informal for 'certainly not!'.
explanation.definitionFit: No fear is a colloquial British exclamation of emphatic refusal, meaning certainly not.

clue.text: Insect has swallowed a tailless rodent, as everybody knows

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a fly is an insect
taken as written

indicators.note: without a tail means the final letter of that creature is dropped

parts.note: a mouse is a rodent

explanation.surface: An insect has gulped down a mouse missing its tail, as is well known.
explanation.walkthrough: The shortened rodent and A go inside the insect, between its F and LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Famously means in a well-known way, so something everyone is aware of.

clue.text: African city building to repair

indicators.note: building means constructing, so these letters are put together in a new form

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Buildings in an African city need fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building to repair' reads as one phrase, but building is the signal and the next two words are the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretoria is South Africa's administrative capital.

clue.text: Delegate again wants animal restrained by lead

indicators.note: something restrained is held in, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: to reign is to rule or lead
an ass is an animal

explanation.surface: A delegate asks again for an animal to be kept on a lead.
explanation.walkthrough: Lead sounds like a dog's leash next to animal, but it is the verb, to rule.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassign is to allot a task anew, so to delegate it again.

clue.text: Current unit in outskirts of Hyderabad, incapacitated

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the first and last letters count

parts.note: the first and last letters of Hyderabad
the ampere is the SI unit of electric current

explanation.surface: A power unit on the edge of an Indian city has broken down.
explanation.definitionFit: Hampered means hindered or held back, a synonym for incapacitated in the sense of impeded.

clue.text: Horse briefly ahead of bovine for a day in September, say?

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: equine means of horses, or a horse
an ox is a bovine animal

explanation.surface: A horse runs in front of a cow, apparently on a special day in September.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'say' mark the definition as an example: there is also a March equinox.
explanation.definitionFit: The autumnal equinox falls around 22 or 23 September, when day and night are of equal length.

clue.text: Opening a menu, people polished off cake

indicators.note: polished off means finished or eliminated, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a gate is an opening in a fence or wall
taken as written
taken as written
men are people

explanation.surface: Diners open the menu and wolf down the cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polished off' tempts as 'ate', but it removes the people from menu, leaving U.
explanation.definitionFit: A gâteau is a rich layered cream cake, from the French word for cake.

clue.text: He cuts a pie, deep down

indicators.note: cutting into something means entering it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a tart is a kind of pie
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man slices into a pie.
explanation.definitionFit: At heart and deep down are both idioms for one's true, underlying nature.

clue.text: Rush long-term job?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to hurtle along, out of control
second meaning: one's working life in a profession

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a question about rushing into employment, but the verb and the noun are unrelated senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to move headlong; as a noun it is a profession pursued over a lifetime.

clue.text: Captured by Spain, a Uruguayan island

indicators.note: something captured is held inside, so the answer lies within the following words

parts.note: runs from the end of Spain through a into the start of Uruguayan

explanation.surface: A South American islander is taken prisoner by Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauru is a tiny island republic in the central Pacific.

clue.text: Italian food the pigs ate, almost all chewed up

indicators.note: chewed-up food is mashed out of shape, so these letters are jumbled
almost all means short of the whole, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pigs gobbled up the Italian leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is long thin Italian pasta, a staple food of Italy.

clue.text: A kick, bottom first, not allowed

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom is the end, so the last letter moves to the front

parts.note: taken as written
to boot is to kick

explanation.surface: A kick up the backside is forbidden.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottom suggests a rear end being kicked, but it is the last letter of the phrase moving to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is forbidden by custom or social convention.

clue.text: Antelope nuzzling into nice new flower

indicators.note: nuzzling into something means pushing inside it, so one piece goes within the other
new means made afresh, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: An antelope nuzzles a pleasant, freshly opened flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The celandine is a small yellow wild flower of the buttercup or poppy family.

clue.text: Hike, heading off for walk

indicators.note: a heading is the top of a word, so taking it off drops the first letter

parts.note: a ramble is a hike in the countryside

explanation.surface: Hikers set off on a walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' sounds like setting out, but it removes the head of the hike word.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow, relaxed pace.

clue.text: Lover gone, one helping to find forgiveness

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
taken as written
a ration is a portion, a helping

explanation.surface: After a lover has left, someone seeks a way to forgive.
explanation.definitionFit: Exoneration is release from blame, close in sense to pardon or forgiveness.
